tagline: The catalog of every software system you build — which customer it's for, which GitHub repos make it up, and one-click repo creation from your templates.
summary: Code Control is the source of truth for software systems: a named product or workspace, tied to a customer, with its list of GitHub repos. From a system's page you can create new repos from your own template repos (Express, Next.js web, Python, React Native) or link repos that already exist. Other Luckee apps — Code Commit Summaries in particular — read their project list from here.

It's built as three pieces. The web app talks to an Express API that has no database connection of its own; every read and write is forwarded to a storage server that owns the `code_control` Postgres, either directly or through the studio's main gateway (on-device dispatcher). Customers aren't stored here at all — they're read from My Ops Tracker's CRM through the same gateway.
audience: You run a studio or freelance practice and start new repos for customers from a set of templates.
You want one list of software systems that other tools (commit summaries, dashboards) can rely on.
You already run the studio stack: on-device dispatcher and My Ops Tracker.
notFor: A code generator — the old codegen tables were dropped (`091_drop_codegen.sql`); it creates repos from templates, nothing more.
Managing customers or engagements — those live in My Ops Tracker; Code Control only reads them.
Running standalone without the storage server — the API can't reach Postgres by itself.

capabilities.title: Software systems
capabilities.detail: `/software-systems` and `/software-system-detail-page` list systems and their linked repos (`software_systems`, `software_system_repos`).

capabilities.title: Create repos from templates
capabilities.detail: Create Express, web, Python or React Native repos in an allowed GitHub org from your template repos, or **link** an existing repo.

capabilities.title: Customers from the CRM
capabilities.detail: `/customers` and `/customer-detail-page` show customers read from My Ops Tracker via `GET /api/crm/*`; a sync modal reconciles names.

capabilities.title: Dashboard with stack check
capabilities.detail: `/dashboard` shows a setup gate until the API reports storage and Postgres healthy.

capabilities.title: Gateway-friendly storage
capabilities.detail: The storage server exposes `POST /api/storage/v1/invoke` plus a dispatcher exposed-endpoints list so the studio gateway can route to it.

capabilities.title: Studio seed / migration
capabilities.detail: `POST /api/studio-seed/import-to-local` copies data from a canonical storage into a local one (laptop → studio).

components.name: Web app
components.stack: Next.js, Redux Toolkit, Tailwind, Luxon (Supabase auth scaffold only)
components.owns: UI for software systems, repo setup and customers. Next.js rewrites `/api/*` to `CODE_CONTROL_API_URL`. No login required locally.

components.name: API
components.owns: HTTP routes for software systems and repo setup, GitHub template repo creation (PAT), the CRM proxy to My Ops Tracker, health of the storage chain.
components.doesNotOwn: SQL — every `src/data` function calls the storage server's `invoke` with the same function name.

components.name: Storage server
components.runsOn: The machine that owns the `code_control` database (port 3080), normally the studio
components.owns: The Postgres schema in `migrations/`, all SQL, `v1/invoke`, seed export/import, dispatcher exposed endpoints.

dataFlow: The browser calls Next.js `/api/*`, which rewrites to the Express API.

Express forwards CRUD to storage: **direct** (`CODE_CONTROL_DIRECT_URL` + secret, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:3080`) or through the **studio gateway** (`MAIN_GATEWAY_URL` + `MAIN_GATEWAY_PROJECT_ID` + `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET`).
Storage runs the matching SQL against local Postgres `code_control`.
Customer reads go Express → main gateway → My Ops Tracker storage (`OPS_TRACKER_GATEWAY_PROJECT_ID=my-ops-tracker`).
Repo creation calls the GitHub API with the PAT on Express and records the new repo on the software system.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: No secrets. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` only (API URL, allowed orgs, optional Supabase anon key).

trust.title: API machine
trust.detail: Holds the GitHub PAT and the storage / gateway secrets. Never holds `DATABASE_URL`.

trust.title: Storage host
trust.detail: Only place with `DATABASE_URL`. Postgres binds to 127.0.0.1; the storage server accepts only callers with `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET`.

trust.title: Studio gateway
trust.detail: Authenticates with `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET` and only forwards endpoints listed as exposed.

commonTasks.title: Run everything on one machine
commonTasks.when: Laptop or studio, all three repos local.
steps: On the **Storage Express** repo, **Set up local database** to create `code_control` and apply `migrations/`.

Set `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET` on storage and the same value as `CODE_CONTROL_DIRECT_SECRET` on the API; choose the **Direct storage** data plane with `CODE_CONTROL_DIRECT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3080`.
Set the GitHub PAT and template repo env vars on the API (see the OSS quickstart).
Press **Run**; `curl <api>/api/health` should show storage and database `ok`.

commonTasks.title: Use the studio's data from a laptop
commonTasks.when: Canonical storage runs on the studio Mac.
steps: Pick the **Studio gateway** data plane on the API.
You don't need to run the storage repo locally.

commonTasks.title: Start a new software system
commonTasks.when: A new product or customer build.
steps: Make sure the customer exists in My Ops Tracker.
Create the software system for that customer in `/software-systems`.
On its detail page, create the repos you need from templates or link existing ones.

commonTasks.title: Connect your GitHub org and templates
commonTasks.when: First time, or moving to a new org.
steps: Create template repos (Express, web, etc.) in your org and mark them as GitHub templates.
Set the PAT, allowed owners and template names on the API per `docs/oss-quickstart.md#connect-github`.
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_ALLOWED_ORGS` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_DEFAULT_ORG` on the web to match.

troubleshooting.symptom: Dashboard stuck on the setup gate / health shows storage down
troubleshooting.fix: The storage server isn't running or the secret doesn't match. Start it and compare `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET` with the API's direct/storage secret.

troubleshooting.symptom: Customers list is empty or errors
troubleshooting.fix: Customers come from My Ops Tracker via the main gateway. Check `MAIN_GATEWAY_URL`, `DISPATCHER_GATE_SECRET` and that my-ops-tracker storage exposes customers.
Check the PAT's scopes, that the target org is allowed, and that the template repo exists and is marked as a template.
`CODE_CONTROL_API_URL` doesn't match the API's port (3012 under Hub, 3010 standalone).

glossary.definition: A product/workspace with its GitHub repos, keyed by a My Ops CRM customer id (formerly `customer_projects`).
code-generator-storage-server — owns Postgres and all SQL; the API calls it via `invoke`.
The studio's on-device dispatcher (port 3010) that routes `/<project-id>/…` to each project's storage.
Customers are read live from My Ops Tracker instead of a local table.

hubNotes: The registry's `expectedTables` (`customers`, `customer_projects`, `customer_project_repos`) are out of date — migration 095 drops `customers` and 096 renames the others to `software_systems` / `software_system_repos`. The database check will report them missing on a current schema.
hub.local.json points `storageExpressDir` at `~/github/code-control/code-generator-storage-server`, while the example file uses `~/luckee/code-control/...`.
The README route table still says `/api/data/projects`; the live routes are `/api/data/software-systems*`.
There's a stray file in `~/github/code-control/` whose name contains a dispatcher gate secret (`x-dispatcher-gate-secret: …`). Delete it and consider rotating that secret.
